# Accordion

Accordion organizes expandable sections inside a native screen while keeping related content in context.

## Import

```tsx
import { Accordion } from '@vellira-ui/react-native';
```

## API

API details are generated from `packages/react-native/API.md`.

| Prop            | Type                                                       | Required | Description                                                                 |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `children`      | `ReactNode`                                                | No       | Content rendered inside the component.                                      |
| `type`          | `'single' \| 'multiple'`                                   | No       | Selection mode: single allows one item, multiple allows several open items. |
| `value`         | `string \| string[]`                                       | No       | Controlled expanded value.                                                  |
| `defaultValue`  | `string \| string[]`                                       | No       | Initial expanded value for uncontrolled usage.                              |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void) \| ((value: string[]) => void)` | No       | Called when the expanded value changes.                                     |
| `collapsible`   | `boolean`                                                  | No       | Allows the open item to collapse in single mode.                            |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                                                  | No       | Disables every accordion item.                                              |

## When To Use

- Settings groups, account details, FAQs, and compact mobile screens.
- Use single mode when only one section should be open.
- Use multiple mode when users may need several sections visible at once.
- Use Tabs when switching between peer screen sections rather than revealing details inline.

## Accessibility

- Accordion.Trigger uses accessibilityRole='button' and exposes expanded and disabled state through accessibilityState.
- React Native does not use DOM attributes such as aria-controls.
- Textual children inside Accordion.Content should be rendered with React Native Text components.
- Verify important accordion flows with VoiceOver and TalkBack on target devices.

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { Text } from 'react-native';

import { Accordion } from '@vellira-ui/react-native';

<Accordion defaultValue='billing'>
  <Accordion.Item value='billing'>
    <Accordion.Trigger>Billing</Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Content>
      <Text>View invoices, payment methods, and plan limits.</Text>
    </Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>

  <Accordion.Item value='security'>
    <Accordion.Trigger>Security</Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Content>
      <Text>Review passkeys, sessions, and recovery options.</Text>
    </Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>
</Accordion>;
```

## Parts

| Part                | Purpose                                         |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `Accordion`         | Root state, selection mode, and disabled state. |
| `Accordion.Item`    | Value-scoped section container.                 |
| `Accordion.Trigger` | Pressable control that toggles an item.         |
| `Accordion.Content` | Panel rendered for the matching item.           |

Use stable string values. Selection is value-based and does not depend on item
render order.

## Single And Multiple Mode

Single mode is the default:

```tsx
<Accordion defaultValue='profile'>...</Accordion>
```

Use multiple mode when several sections may stay open:

```tsx
<Accordion type='multiple' defaultValue={['profile', 'billing']}>
  ...
</Accordion>
```

Multiple mode uses `string[]` for controlled and uncontrolled values.

## Controlled Usage

```tsx
const [section, setSection] = useState('profile');

<Accordion value={section} onValueChange={setSection}>
  ...
</Accordion>;
```

Control the accordion when expansion state belongs to navigation, persistence,
or a parent settings screen.

## Collapsible Behavior

In single mode, activating the open item keeps it open by default. Add
`collapsible` to allow the selected item to close:

```tsx
<Accordion collapsible defaultValue='notifications'>
  ...
</Accordion>
```

Multiple mode does not use `collapsible`; each item can be closed separately.

## Disabled State

```tsx
<Accordion disabled>...</Accordion>

<Accordion.Item value='enterprise' disabled>
  ...
</Accordion.Item>
```

Disabled root state affects every item. Disabled item state affects only that
section.

## React Native Differences

`Accordion.Trigger` renders its label inside a native `Text` component.
`Accordion.Content` is rendered inside a View-like host, so textual content
inside content panels should be wrapped in React Native `Text` components.

React Native does not use DOM attributes such as `aria-controls`. Trigger state
is exposed through native accessibility state instead.

## Accessibility

`Accordion.Trigger` exposes button semantics and expanded state where supported
by the platform. Keep labels short and distinct, avoid nesting unrelated
controls in a trigger, and test important flows with VoiceOver and TalkBack.
